newsitem.title: FINLAND: Hoax delays Finnish phone sale, internet feared.
newsitem.headline: Hoax delays Finnish phone sale, internet feared.

text.p: A fake bid apparently based on information available on the internet has delayed the privatisation of a local Finnish telephone operator, officials said on Wednesday.

The council of the city of Turku on Monday postponed the sale of its telephone operator Turun Puhelin after receiving a fax that apeared to be a bid from Dutch PTT Telecom -- part of Dutch PTT -- but proved later to be an elaborate hoax.

"At first glance, this looks real...but a second read reveals details that show it is not," said director Aatos Hallipelto at investment banking firm PCA Coporate Finance, the city's adviser on the sale.
The phoney offer upped the real bids on all key points, and was quite skillfully written based on documents "that could easiest be obtained via the Internet," Hallipelto said.
The document, two A4 size sheets, arrived on Monday showing PTT Telecom's fax number as the sender, but that number can easily be manipulated, fax manufacturers say.
According to some media reports, experts believe the fax was sent from Finland since its timestamps suggest it was sent in Finland's timezone, one hour ahead of the Netherlands.

Finnish media on Wednesday quoted PTT Telecom officials as saying they did not even know the Finnish company was for sale and dismissed any connection with the offer, pointing to spelling mistakes and differences between the document's forged logo and the original.
Although the authenticity of the surprise bid was met with skepticism, the confusion it created was sufficient to postpone the sale until next month, Hallipelto said.
It was unclear on Wednesday whether police would investigate the incident.
